facts.text: A collision-avoidance system moves a machine from an awareness function to a motion-control safety function.
facts.quote: A collision-avoidance system moves the machine from an awareness function to a motion-control safety function.

facts.text: The second edition of ISO 19014-2 applies to machine control systems that control motion or mitigate a hazard, but excludes awareness-only systems such as cameras and radar detectors.
facts.quote: The second edition of ISO 19014-2 applies to machine control systems that control motion or mitigate a hazard, while awareness-only systems such as cameras and radar detectors are excluded

facts.text: ISO 19014-5 provides performance-level tables for safety-control functions; the source evidence is marked draft.
facts.quote: ISO 19014-5 provides performance-level tables for safety-control functions.

facts.text: ISO showed the second edition of ISO 19014-2 and ISO 19014-5 as under publication in October 2026.

facts.text: The final publication status of the second edition of ISO 19014-2 and ISO 19014-5 should be rechecked before design freeze.

facts.text: Abrupt longitudinal deceleration transfers load and, on a cross-slope or during steering, combines with lateral load transfer, creating rollover or unload-instability hazards.
facts.quote: Abrupt longitudinal deceleration transfers load; on a cross-slope or during steering this combines with lateral load transfer.

facts.text: High-center-of-gravity payloads, partially loaded bodies, suspended tools and uneven ground worsen rollover or unload instability from braking.
facts.quote: High-center-of-gravity payloads, partially loaded bodies, suspended tools and uneven ground worsen it.

facts.text: Overloading makes machinery less stable and less able to steer and brake; this is general safety guidance not separately sourced.
facts.quote: Overloading makes machinery less stable and less able to steer and brake. **Expert opinion** (general safety guidance; not separately sourced).

facts.text: Li et al. model active braking as an influence on wheel-loader roll.
facts.quote: Li et al. model active braking as an influence on wheel-loader roll. **Independent** [30, 46].

facts.text: Braking alters front-unit and rear-unit yaw and articulation dynamics, creating articulation and yaw-instability hazards.
facts.quote: Braking alters front-unit and rear-unit yaw and articulation dynamics

facts.text: Direct quantitative automatic-braking data for off-road articulated haulers were not found.
facts.quote: direct quantitative automatic-braking data for off-road articulated haulers: not found.

facts.text: Draft ISO/PRF 21815-5 has dedicated treatment of articulation-related collision movement, reflecting the need to account for articulation.
facts.quote: The need to account for articulation is reflected in ISO/PRF 21815-5's dedicated treatment of articulation-related collision movement.

facts.text: Using all available ground shear for longitudinal braking leaves less lateral capability for steering, so braking as hard as physically possible is unsafe in some turning and cross-slope cases.
facts.quote: Using the available ground shear fully for longitudinal braking leaves less lateral capability for steering, so "brake as hard as physically possible" is unsafe in some turning and cross-slope cases.

facts.text: The New South Wales braking formulas explicitly assume no skidding.
facts.quote: The New South Wales formulas explicitly assume no skidding

facts.text: ISO 3450 includes controllability requirements during braking.
facts.quote: ISO 3450 includes controllability requirements during braking.

facts.text: For off-road automatic braking, the load or attachment can set the binding limit before traction is exhausted; a rock-filled dumper, a lifted loader bucket and an unloaded dozer need different envelopes.
facts.quote: The binding limit can be set by the load or attachment before traction is exhausted: a rock-filled dumper, a lifted loader bucket and an unloaded dozer need different envelopes.

facts.text: Published data and universal braking limits for configurations such as a rock-filled dumper, a lifted loader bucket and an unloaded dozer were not found.
facts.quote: Published data and universal limits for such configurations: not found.

facts.text: At a dump edge or excavation, braking loads add to already marginal ground support, creating sliding or ground-failure hazards.
facts.quote: At a dump edge or excavation, braking loads add to already marginal ground support.

facts.text: NIOSH mining research has included braking inertial forces in slope-edge stability analysis, but a specific source was not found.
facts.quote: NIOSH mining research has included braking inertial forces in slope-edge stability analysis (specific source not found).

facts.text: MSHA engineers estimate that three to four miners' lives could be saved each year if adequate seat belts were provided and worn.

facts.text: Operator restraint matters for an automatic stop because sudden stops can injure operators.
facts.quote: *Operator injury from sudden stops.* MSHA engineers estimate that "three to four miners' lives could be saved each year if adequate seat belts were provided and worn", which is also why restraint matters for an automatic stop.

facts.text: Unexpected automatic deceleration from false positives can create conflict with following plant or cause an operator to lose control.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 recommends requiring an operator action, such as applying the parking brake, before automatic brake release where needed to prevent rollaway.
